::: {#exm-two-level-normal}
#### A two-level Gaussian model

Observations $Y_{ij}$ come from groups $j = 1, \ldots, J$,
and each group has its own mean $\param_j$.
A two-level model specifies

$$
\ba
Y_{ij} \mid \param_j &\sim \ndist{\param_j,\, \sdpar^2}
&& \text{(data given group means)}\\
\param_j \mid \mean, \sdbetween &\sim \ndist{\mean,\, \sdbetween^2}
&& \text{(group means given hyperparameters)}.
\ea
$$

The group means $\param_j$ are the group-level parameters,
and $\mean$ and $\sdbetween$ are the [hyperparameters](#def-hyperparameter).
To fit this model by Bayesian inference,
we add a [hyperprior](#def-hyperprior) for $(\mean, \sdbetween)$
and a prior for the within-group standard deviation $\sdpar$.
:::
